isolation_controls.detail: This branch is a clone at ~/Downloads/sdinv-jhep, outside iCloud and outside the other session's tree. No file is shared; nothing either session writes lands in the other's checkout.

run_rank81_cell.py writes results/rank81/cells/cell_p{p}_s{seed}.json, one file per cell, never a shared summary. The older loop rewrote a single certificate.json after every cell, which is how a partial run could overwrite a complete one.
Each cell is written to a temporary file in the same directory and moved into place with os.replace, so a reader never sees a half-written cell and a crash cannot truncate a good one.
A second driver for the same cell finds the lock, prints who holds it, and exits 2 rather than racing.
A cell already marked cell_complete is skipped unless --force, so re-running the matrix cannot downgrade a finished result.

assemble_rank81_matrix.py only reads cells. It fails on a missing cell, a duplicate, a candidate-ordering difference, a coordinate-dimension difference or an incomplete terminal status, rather than assembling something partial into a certificate.
Push is the only operation that can actually race, and it is held until the final reconciliation.

concurrency_policy: The other session was left running by an explicit decision: reconcile at the end rather than interrupt work in flight. Isolation, not termination, is what makes this safe, and the controls that provide it are listed above. Push is deferred to the final reconciliation because it is the only operation that races.
